claim: The MMR vaccine causes autism in children.
rationale: Wakefield et al. 1998, retracted by The Lancet in 2010 for fraud; a retracted source cannot support any claim.

claim: Hydroxychloroquine increases in-hospital mortality in COVID-19 patients, per a large multinational registry.
rationale: Mehra et al. 2020 (Surgisphere), retracted after the underlying registry could not be verified.

claim: Somatic cells can be reprogrammed to pluripotency by brief exposure to a low-pH stress (STAP).
rationale: Obokata et al. 2014 STAP paper, retracted by Nature; results were not reproducible and showed manipulation.

claim: A tissue-engineered, stem-cell-seeded tracheobronchial scaffold restored durable airway function in a transplant patient.
rationale: Macchiarini et al. 2011, retracted amid misconduct findings; outcomes were misrepresented.

claim: Beta-carotene is essential for the assembly of photosystem II.
rationale: Zakar et al. 2016 conclusion states verbatim: 'beta-carotene is essential for the assembly of PSII'. Open-access full text.

claim: Carotenoids photoprotect photosystem II by deactivating triplet chlorophyll and singlet oxygen.
rationale: Jahns & Holzwarth 2011 abstract: carotenoids 'deactivate triplet chlorophyll and singlet oxygen'. Abstract-level support (confidence should be capped).

claim: Carotenoids transfer absorbed light energy to chlorophyll in the light-harvesting complex of photosystem II.
rationale: Gradinaru et al. 1997 abstract reports direct evidence of energy transfer from carotenoid to chlorophyll b in LHC II.

claim: Zeaxanthin is the major xanthophyll driving non-photochemical quenching in photosystem II.
rationale: Same review abstract: 'zeaxanthin is the major player ... in NPQ (non-photochemical quenching)'.

claim: A beta-carotene in the photosystem II reaction centre enables a secondary electron-transfer pathway that protects P680.
rationale: Telfer 2003 abstract establishes a photoprotective role via P680-triplet quenching and singlet-oxygen scavenging, not an electron-transfer pathway; the claim asserts a mechanism the source does not support.

claim: Carotenoids are the sole determinant of photosystem II stability.
rationale: The paper says carotenoids assist and xanthophylls can stabilize PSII; 'sole determinant' overstates a contributory role.

claim: Carotenoids are not required for photosystem II assembly.
rationale: Directly contradicts the cited paper, whose conclusion states beta-carotene is essential for PSII assembly.
Telfer 2003 is about beta-carotene in photosystem II; it does not address human vision, so the text cannot establish the claim either way.
The DOI is the carotenoid/PSII paper, but the cited (expected) title is a different paper; citation integrity should fail (title mismatch) even though the DOI's own content supports the claim.

claim: t-SNE visualisations of single-cell data can distort global structure, so apparent distances between well-separated clusters should not be over-interpreted.
rationale: Kobak & Berens 2019 (Nat Commun, open access with a results section) cautions exactly this about t-SNE for single-cell transcriptomics.

claim: A reef dominated by encrusting, slow-growing, small-bodied corals is not ecologically equivalent to one dominated by branching, tabular, or massive reef-builders, even when total cover is similar.
rationale: Alvarez-Filip et al. 2013 (open access) shows replacing major reef-builders with small opportunists sharply reduces calcification and rugosity independent of total cover; the negated claim is established. (Independently confirmed SUPPORTED by Manusights.)

claim: Vitamin D supplementation reduced the risk of acute respiratory tract infection, with an adjusted odds ratio of about 0.88.
rationale: Martineau et al. 2017 (BMJ, open access) reports aOR 0.88 (95% CI 0.81-0.96) for acute respiratory infection; '~0.88' is within rounding, so numeric leeway should rule SUPPORTED.

claim: Carotenoids protect photosystem II against oxidative damage.
rationale: Zakar et al. 2016 states carotenoids protect against over-excitation and oxidative side products; the claim is a paraphrase of this, so meaning-not-wording should rule SUPPORTED.

claim: Carotenoids are essential for photosystem II assembly and increase crop yield.
rationale: The paper supports the assembly half but says nothing about crop yield (it studies cyanobacterial PSII); the claim conjoins a supported part with an unsupported one, so it overreaches.
